item.title: Artist Talk: Caroline Kent — Thu Nov 12, 5:30 PM — UC Davis
item.description:
Caroline Kent — who develops art through an open-ended archive of improvisational works on paper — will give a talk on Thursday, Nov. 12 as part of the Visiting Artist Lecture Series in the Maria Manetti Shrem Art Studio Program. In her work, Kent labors to expand the discourse of modernist abstraction by questioning how language might operate in unknown and ever-evolving conditions. A 2025 USA Fellow and a recipient of the Aspen Arts Prize for innovation in painting, she has received grants from the Pollock-Krasner Foundation, The McKnight Foundation, and Jerome Foundation. She was a 2020 Artadia Chicago Awardee and a 2021 Joyce Alexander Wein Prize recipient from the Studio Museum in Harlem. Recent exhibitions include La Trienal at El Museo del Barrio, New York, and Ancestral at the Museum of Brazilian Art (M.A.B.), Sao Paulo, Brazil.
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Book Release: What Has the World Come To? — Thu Nov 12, 6:30 PM — Mary L. Stephens Davis Branch Library
item.description:
The Culture C.O.-O.P., in collaboration with Mary L. Stephens Davis Library, would like to warmly welcome you to an upcoming book release. Join us for this gathering featuring Sandy Holman, author of What Has the World Come To?, and young professionals, where attendance is open to all members of the public, with a free digital copy to those who attend! What Has the World Come To? is a collection of short stories designed as an entry point for healing, reflection, and inspiring change. These stories are formatted to take readers through a journey. Beginning with Reckoning, then establishing Foundations, continued with passing through Memoriam. The shorts then follow through Anchoring to ultimately rest in Gratitude. Once again, please feel free to join us in the celebration of this book release. The chance to gain new perspectives can give you the tools to succeed!
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Out of Line: Art at the Edge — Fri Nov 13, 10:00 AM — Jan Shrem and Maria Manetti Shrem Museum of Art at UC Davis
item.description:
Inspired by conceptual artist Bruce Nauman’s video work “Dance or Exercise on the Perimeter of a Square (Square Dance), 1967–68,” this exhibition explores Davis as a site of both artistic practice and political protest. Mike Henderson, Ester Hernandez, Malaquías Montoya, Bruce Nauman, Nancy Rubins, Dorothy Wiley and the student artists of UC Davis’ Third World Forum engage with film, print and performance to confront who they were and what their work meant in a world of radical change. They made work wherever and however they could: in collaborative workshops, student newsrooms, kitchens and living rooms. While rooted in the politics of the late 20th century, “Out of Line” finds renewed meaning in the present day.
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Together Again, 1960–2026: Perspectives from UC Davis' Fine Arts Collection — Fri Nov 13, 10:00 AM — Jan Shrem and Maria Manetti Shrem Museum of Art at UC Davis
item.description:
This ongoing collection exhibition traces a history of art forged from this place. By focusing on relationships of many kinds, “Together Again” proposes that in order to understand an artwork in all its fullness, chance encounters and long-standing friendships often matter as much as formal affiliations. UC Davis legends such as Wayne Thiebaud, Deborah Butterfield and Bruce Nauman are exhibited alongside important regional voices that were once overlooked, and the exhibition extends to the artists shaping Northern California today, including Sadie Barnette, Woody De Othello and Ruby Neri.
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Human Relations Commission Meetings — Thu Nov 26, 6:30 PM — City Hall Community Chambers
item.description:
The Davis Human Relations Commission (HRC) meetings aim to promote mutual respect, understanding, justice, and advancing the human rights of all people. The Human Relations Commission meets on the fourth Thursday of each month at 6:30 p.m. The Commission takes a recess in July (no meeting in July).
Meetings take place in the Community Chambers at City Hall, 23 Russell Boulevard. For more information on meetings, membership, resolutions, and more, visit the Human Relations Commission site.
The HRC makes recommendations around equity and discrimination in the City, and supports the City in preventing and addressing discrimination while promoting diversity, equality, and justice relevant to the goals and policies of the City Council.
To contact or send emails to the commission, email: HRC@cityofdavis.org
Source: Hate-Free Together

The event is for students, by students, and is FREE! Come and one-stop-shop the best places to live in Davis for the coming year. All are welcome including undergraduates, graduate/professional students as well as members of the public.
At every Housing Fair, we host over 50 apartment complex managers and resource representatives. This staff helps answer your pressing questions as well as make sure you find a place that is aligned with your needs and wants. Housing Fair is filled not only with an array of information, but with swag and prizes! We hope to see you at our next Fair!
Source: UC Davis CampusGroups

item.title: Davis Farmers Market – Wednesday Evenings (50th Anniversary Year) — Wed Jan 27, 3:00 PM — Central Park
item.description:
The Davis Farmers Market continues every Wednesday in Central Park with new fall hours! Beginning Wednesday, September 2, the Wednesday market will be open from 3:00–6:00 PM, replacing the extended 4:00–8:00 PM Picnic in the Park hours. Stop by to shop for fresh, locally grown produce, artisan goods, prepared foods and other market favorites from local farmers and vendors. It’s a great opportunity to stock up for the week, meet up with friends, support local growers and food makers, and enjoy a beautiful afternoon in Central Park. The Davis Farmers Market is celebrating its 50th Anniversary in 2026, marking five decades of bringing fresh food, local farmers and the Davis community together. Wednesday Market Details:
Wednesdays from 3:00–6:00 PM Central Park in Downtown Davis Fresh, seasonal produce Artisan goods and prepared foods Local farmers and food makers Family-friendly and open to everyone
Free to attend – shop local and enjoy your Wednesday afternoon at the Davis Farmers
